shared_elements: circle/disc motif (central boss in A; row of loop/disc-like forms at top of B)
a band of repeated geometric units running across the field (ring of oval perforations in A; register of rectangles and zigzags in B)
stylised creature with symmetrically splayed limbs (central arachnid/beetle-like form in A; splayed animal figures in B)
radial/repeated marginal projections (toothed rim in A; row of vertical strokes/legs in B)
justification: Both are stone reliefs that combine a repeated geometric register with a stylised, symmetrically splayed creature and disc-like elements, which is the most specific correspondence. But A is a self-contained, radially symmetric circular disc organised in concentric rings around a central boss, whereas B is a tall rectangular pillar with stacked horizontal registers of profile animals, so the compositional logic and the modelling (crisp incised geometry versus soft rounded relief) differ fundamentally.
